entries.title: Genesis 41:1
segments: The river; the Nile, upon the annual overflow of which the fertility of Egypt depends.

entries.title: Genesis 41:2
segments:
Kine; cows. 
 
  Well-favored; good looking.  So ill-favored means bad looking. Both the fat and the lean cows came out of the river, signifying that from it come both plenty and want in Egypt.

entries.title: Genesis 41:5
segments: Ears of corn; heads of wheat.  The so called Egyptian wheat bears several heads on one stalk.

entries.title: Genesis 41:7
segments: All future things are known to God, and as far as he sees best he makes them known to men.  Before men had the Bible, God often communicated information to them in dreams and visions.  But now we are not to expect information in those ways, but to give heed to the Bible, which is able to make us wise unto salvation, and furnish us thoroughly for every good work.

entries.title: Genesis 41:8
segments: Magicians; the sacred scribes of Egypt, whose office was to explain signs, interpret dreams, and reveal hidden things.

entries.title: Genesis 41:9
segments: My faults; against Pharaoh, rather than against Joseph.

entries.title: Genesis 41:13
segments: He restored; Pharaoh restored.  The chief butler speaks of his maonarch in the third person.

entries.title: Genesis 41:14
segments: God never overlooks the trials of his people, or suffers them to continue a moment too long.  When the right time comes he delivers them, often suddenly, in ways, by means, and for purposes which they never expected.

entries.title: Genesis 41:16
segments:
It is not in me; he could not of himself interpret the dream, it must be by divine aid. 
 
  An answer of peace; one that would remove his fears and promote his good.

entries.title: Genesis 41:25
segments:
Is one; both dreams mean the same thing. 
 
Those who in all their ways acknowledge God, will find that he directs their paths; and those things which they thought to be against them, they will see were ordered in such a way as to promote their highest good.

entries.title: Genesis 41:26
segments: Are seven years; represent them.

entries.title: Genesis 41:28
segments: This is the thing which I have spoken; this is the thing which I said before.  See

entries.title: Genesis 41:33
segments: The fact that men are dependent on God does not supersede the necessity, on their part, of wisdom and discretion; and those who have most of these qualities, will be most likely to be successful.

entries.title: Genesis 41:34
segments: Of the land; the produce of the land.

entries.title: Genesis 41:36
segments: The land perish not; the inhabitants of it.

entries.title: Genesis 41:39
segments: Those who know most of God and his ways will be the most wise and discreet.  They can be most safely trusted, and in great and difficult services may be expected to do the most good.

entries.title: Genesis 41:42
segments: Put it upon Joseph's hand; in token of his being clothed with authority.

entries.title: Genesis 41:43
segments: The second chariot; the chariot assigned to the man that stood next in rank to the king, and doubtless second to the king's chariot in splendor.

entries.title: Genesis 41:44
segments:
Lift up his hand or foot; a proverbial expression, denoting that all the people should be under Joseph's control. 
 
He who shows the most kindness, patience, compassion, and benevolence in a dungeon, may be expected to show the most humility, meekness, equanimity, and loveliness on a throne.

entries.title: Genesis 41:45
segments:
Zaphnath-paaneah; supposed to mean, saviour of the world. 
 
  Priest; a priest at that time, in Egypt, was a civil as well as an ecclesiastical ruler; and by this marriage Joseph became connected with one of the great men of the kingdom. 
 
  On; called by the Greeks Heliopolis, or the city of the sun.  It was on the east of the Nile, in the land of Goshen, and not far from the modern Cairo.

entries.title: Genesis 41:47
segments: By handfuls; in great abundance.

entries.title: Genesis 41:48
segments: Laid up the food; that which was not wanted for present use.

entries.title: Genesis 41:51
segments: Manasseh; that is, one causing forgetfulness.

entries.title: Genesis 41:52
segments:
Ephraim; fruitful. 
 
God can, in this world, cause his people to forget their sorrows, or so to remember them as to heighten their joys, and make them feel that their sharpest trials were not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall follow.

entries.title: Genesis 41:55
segments: Egypt was famished; the people had consumed all their food, and were in want.
